articles.title: Who is vfmaddrnd231pd?
articles.summary: vfmaddrnd231pd is a unique instruction from the FMA instruction set, defined in the Intel Software Development Manual as VFMADDRND231PD - Fused Multiply-Add of Packed Double-Precision Floating-Point Values with rounding control. This instruction allows for controlled rounding of floating-point values, potentially making some algorithms faster. However, it appears that the instruction is not recognized by GNU assembler, the Intel C/C++ Compiler, or other tools, and its implementation is not available in recent versions of the Software Development Manual.

articles.title: Parsing JSON at tens of gigabytes per second… in Python

The GH Archive project collects these events as JSON, one event per line, one file per hour. I took eight hours of March 13, 2024: 7.6 GB of JSON once decompressed, 2.2 million events. I want to know which programming languages get the most new pull requests. I count the events by type, and for each pull request that was opened, I look up the language of the repository. Each event is a large JSON object, about 3.4 kB on average. I need only a few of its fields. The answer, for these eight hours, is 65,269 pull requests were opened, mostly toward TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Java repositories.
